findings.issue: The round-3 on_start mechanism targets the WRONG dispatch path. The spec routes on_start entry through FunnelEventService: change (a) relax FunnelService.validateTriggers requireNoEntryStep for on_start, change (b) FunnelEventService.matchedEntryStepId returns the on_start trigger's entryStepId. But /start is NOT dispatched through FunnelEventService at all. ProcessTelegramUpdateJob.java:311 calls funnelTriggerService.fire(projectId, chatId, "on_start", startPayload), which lands in FunnelTriggerServiceImpl.fire() (lines 121-188). fire() hardcodes the start cursor to step 0 via executionFactory.insertExecution(..., 0) on BOTH branches (lines 171 and 177) and never reads any entryStepId. Independently, matchedEntryStepId short-circuits to null for every non-event trigger (FunnelEventService.java:289 `if (!TRIGGER_EVENT.equals(triggerType)) return null;`), and on_start is never even passed to dispatchForSubscriber. So both named point changes compile but are INERT for on_start enrollment: change (b) is reachable only for `event` triggers; the on_start /start path bypasses it entirely.
findings.why_matters: The acceptance criterion 'on_start заводить підписника у крок, на який указує ребро стартового вузла, незалежно від позиції цього кроку в масиві' (lines 114-115, 124-126) depends entirely on this. With the mechanism as written, /start still enrolls at array[0] regardless of the drawn start edge — the array-order-irrelevance claim for on_start does NOT hold. This is the same defect class flagged in round 2 (resolveStartCursor receives a null startStepId for on_start): the seam was renamed from resolveStartCursor to FunnelEventService.matchedEntryStepId, but it still names a code path that the on_start /start trigger never traverses. resolveStartCursor itself is fine (it already honors a non-null start, FunnelExecutionFactory.java:117-126) — the gap is that nothing feeds it a non-null start for on_start.
findings.fix: Re-point the mechanism at the ACTUAL on_start seam: FunnelTriggerServiceImpl.fire(). After fire() resolves the matched funnel (line 160), re-scan that funnel's triggers[] for the on_start element (mirroring matchedEntryStepId's event re-scan), read its entryStepId, and call executionFactory.insertExecutionAt(projectId, funnel, subscriberId, telegramBotId, 0, entryStepId) instead of insertExecution(..., 0) on BOTH branches (lines 171 and 177). resolveStartCursor needs no change (correct in the spec). KEEP change (a) (relax requireNoEntryStep so on_start can persist entryStepId). DROP change (b) (matchedEntryStepId is the event/dispatchForSubscriber path, irrelevant to on_start; leaving it would be dead code). Update Ограничения (on_start bullet, lines 152-161), Технические решения (line 210-215), Risk 4 (lines 191-195), and Тестирование/engine-IT (lines 241-246) to name fire()/insertExecutionAt as the seam — not FunnelEventService.matchedEntryStepId.

findings.issue: The change is mis-scoped: the spec names two edits in FunnelService + FunnelEventService, but the real on_start fix touches a THIRD file the spec never mentions (FunnelTriggerServiceImpl.fire) and requires NEW logic that does not exist today. fire() currently does findFirst() on the matched funnel (line 160) and never re-scans triggers[] to identify which on_start element matched — so reading its entryStepId means adding a matched-element re-scan (plus a step-0 fallback when the on_start element has no entryStepId, i.e. legacy bare /start). The dispatch architecture deliberately splits on_start (chatId-keyed fire()) from event/tag/field (subscriber-keyed dispatchForSubscriber); the code comments call this out explicitly (FunnelEventService class-doc; fire() lines 142-143 'on_start enrolls always START at step 0'). The spec's mechanism elides this split.
findings.why_matters: Underestimating the touchpoint surface mis-sizes the change and risks an implementer wiring change (b) (inert) and shipping a feature that silently enrolls at step 0 while believing the spec was satisfied. Round 2 already warned that 'exactly two point changes' was either false or self-contradictory; round 3 picked the entry-step-carrier option (correct direction) but still routed it through a seam on_start never reaches, so the scope is still understated.
findings.fix: List FunnelTriggerServiceImpl.fire() as a touched file. Describe the required matched-on_start-element re-scan in fire() and the step-0 fallback when the on_start element carries no entryStepId. Confirm the engine-IT 'on_start із entryStepId заходить у крок-ціль ребра незалежно від order' exercises the fire()/on_start path (not a dispatchForSubscriber/event path), or it will pass while the real /start path stays broken.

findings.issue: The advanceToNext null=end-of-branch change (change (1), lines 145-146, 186-189) is genuinely required and correctly scoped to one method, BUT it is a behavioural REPLACEMENT, not an additive branch. FunnelExecutionEngine.advanceToNext (lines 489-508) today already falls through to snapshot.get(here+1) when next is null (lines 496-502); 'end of graph' only triggers at the last list position (lines 503-507). To make null-next = end-of-branch, the lines 496-502 fall-through block must be REMOVED so a null next sets currentStepId=null unconditionally (gated by graphMode — legacy index-drain snapshots must stay unaffected). The change also flows into advancePastDelay (delay/timeout resume reuses advanceToNext, lines 513-521), which is the desired consistent behaviour but a second path touched by the 'one' edit.
findings.why_matters: If an implementer reads change (1) as additive rather than as deleting the lines 496-502 fall-through, the array-order-still-matters bug persists for mid-array nodes — defeating the core canvas premise. Naming it a replacement (and noting the delay-resume path + graphMode gate) prevents a no-op edit.
findings.fix: Reword change (1) to state the existing default-next-by-list-position fall-through in advanceToNext (~lines 496-502) is REMOVED so null next = end-of-branch unconditionally in graphMode (legacy index-drain runs unaffected via graphMode probe). Note the delay/timeout-resume path (advancePastDelay) is intentionally covered by the same change, and have the engine-IT pin a null-next DELAY/timeout step too.

summary: Round-3 changes_required. The round-2 critical (on_start seam) is still unresolved: the renamed mechanism (relax requireNoEntryStep + matchedEntryStepId returns entryStepId) targets FunnelEventService, but /start on_start is dispatched via FunnelTriggerServiceImpl.fire() (ProcessTelegramUpdateJob:311), which hardcodes step 0 and never reads entryStepId — and matchedEntryStepId short-circuits to null for non-event triggers anyway. Both named changes are inert for on_start, so the array-order-irrelevance claim for on_start does not hold. The real fix lives in fire() (re-scan the on_start element + insertExecutionAt), a file the spec omits. resolveStartCursor and the Trigger.entryStepId round-trip are correct as stated; the advanceToNext null=end change is the right direction but is a replacement (not additive) and must be reworded. canvasPosition/notes design remains sound.
